sections.name: File setup, DEMO_SAMPLES, DemoState
sections.title: Demo constants and step names
sections.what: Names the storage key and the two bundled sample files, and imports the saved-route helper used for links.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the storage name and sample list in one place.
sections.watch_out: The sample list must match the actual files on the server.

sections.name: demoState, startDemo
sections.title: Reading and starting the demo
sections.what: Reads the saved demo state from session storage, returning nothing if the data is missing or damaged. Starting the demo writes an empty project list to that storage.
sections.why: Likely reason: a damaged value should not crash the page.
sections.watch_out: The rest of the app uses this state to decide whether the demo is active, so a broken value silently turns the demo off.

sections.name: rememberDemoProjects, endDemo
sections.title: Remembering projects and ending the demo
sections.what: Stores the list of project IDs created during the demo, but only if a demo is active. Ending the demo removes the stored state.
sections.why: Likely reason: the project IDs let the demo link to the first project later.
sections.watch_out: Projects are not saved if no demo is active, so the first project link may be missing.

sections.name: loadDemoFiles, Stage
sections.title: Loading the bundled sample files
sections.what: Downloads both sample files from the server at the same time and wraps each in a file object, reporting the sample name if one fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: the demo uses real files so it exercises the same path as a user upload.
sections.watch_out: If either download fails, the whole load fails and no file is processed.

sections.name: STEPS
sections.title: Demo step text
sections.what: Stores the title and body text for the four stages, including what the samples contain and what each screen shows.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains each step in plain words while the real pipeline runs.
sections.watch_out: The text names specific counts and file types, so it must be edited when the samples change.

sections.name: DemoTour
sections.title: Demo side panel and buttons
sections.what: Shows the current step number, title and text, plus buttons that depend on the stage, such as building the combined 3D view, downloading the IFC package, opening the first project, going back, or ending the demo.
sections.why: Likely reason: each stage offers only the next useful action.
sections.watch_out: The panel shows nothing without an active demo, and the buttons appear only when the needed job ID or project ID exists.

summary: A guided walkthrough panel that explains the four demo steps and records in the browser session that a demo is running.
purpose: Helps a new viewer understand each stage of the demo while it runs on bundled sample files.
why: Likely reason: session storage keeps the demo state for one browser tab, so it ends when the tab closes.
how: Starting the demo saves a marker in session storage. Loading the demo fetches two bundled sample files from the server. Each stage then shows its title, text and buttons. Ending the demo removes the marker and reloads the page.
inputs: Sample file names, the current stage, an optional saved job ID, and an optional function for the next step.
outputs: A side panel with step text and buttons, plus the two sample files passed on for processing.
risks: With no marker, the panel shows nothing. Damaged stored data is caught and treated as no demo. The step text states specific counts such as three projects from two files, so changed samples would make that text wrong.
debug: If the panel does not appear, check the browser's session storage for the demo key. If samples fail to load, the error names the sample and its HTTP status, so check that the server has that file.
